$comment: Project-owned verification gates for NexaGear. JSON rather than YAML so the runner needs no parser dependency. Mirrors .forge/schemas/verification.cue #VerificationCheck. Only commands listed here are ever executed.

gates.summary: TypeScript strict type check emits no errors.
ESLint reports zero problems and zero warnings.
Vitest suite passes. Includes tests/theme.test.ts, which parses the pre-paint theme/scheme script and executes it, so a syntax error there cannot ship silently.

Every colour pairing the UI renders clears its WCAG threshold in all four theme-by-scheme combinations, and every audited hex is confirmed present in app/globals.css so the numbers cannot describe a palette the site does not use.
Production Next.js build succeeds and emits all routes.
Playwright critical-journey test plus the axe scan of all four theme-and-scheme combinations. Skipped unless FORGE_E2E=1 because it needs a running dev server.

The custom `apple:` Tailwind variant and the [data-theme="apple"] token block are present in the compiled CSS. Tailwind drops an unknown variant silently, so without this the theme can build, pass, and do nothing.
Both dark-scheme token blocks and the color-scheme declarations survive compilation. The dark palettes live only in CSS, so nothing else in the build would notice if they were dropped.
Every product image paints a visible range and real shading, and inverts between light and dark. Needs a running dev server, so it is gated with the e2e check rather than run on every verify.
No secret values appear in the built client bundle; only publishable keys and variable names are permitted.
